title: rest: `GET /data/OBJECT/export?format=json` writes its opening bracket before the first read, so a refused query arrives as a truncated JSON stream instead of a 400
body:
domain:server#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUCizoYWQVJWjhdR6F

Found by the #27484 dev (os-dev-reports `6499580381` and `6503706236`, `out_of_scope_findings`) and escalated by the contract review of PR #27670, record `6504124784` (should-fix S3: an acceptance note is not a carrier).

## What is wrong

The export route in `packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts` streams `format=json` by writing the opening `[` (and the response headers) before its first `findData` call. Any refusal that `findData` raises on the first page therefore arrives after a 200 has started: the client receives a truncated JSON stream instead of the 400 envelope. `format=csv` and `format=xlsx` answer the envelope, because they read before they write.

Reproduce on any object: `GET /api/v1/data/OBJECT/export?format=json&search=x&searchFields=nope` (an unknown search field, refused by the protocol door today). Compare with `format=csv`, which answers 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

## Expected

The json export reads its first page before it writes any byte, so a refusal on that page answers the same 400 envelope the csv and xlsx paths answer. A refusal on a later page (mid-stream) is a separate question and out of this card unless triage widens it.

Filed without `domain:*`; grading is triage's.
